docs/02-product-spec.md:7:## 1. What Axylo is
docs/02-product-spec.md:13:Speed is a constraint, not the headline: Axylo must stay within the budgets in section 5 with default options. Whether it can do that at a million points with its accessibility layer on is something the first milestone measures, not something this document can promise.
docs/02-product-spec.md:15:### 1.1 Why someone would choose it
docs/02-product-spec.md:23:| Highcharts | The best reader experience of the ten | The same class of accessibility with no module to import and no commercial license; reduced-motion support; errors that name the field and the row |
docs/02-product-spec.md:24:| ECharts or ApexCharts | Many chart types | Fewer types, each of which fits its labels, reports bad data and is accessible by default |
docs/02-product-spec.md:25:| uPlot | The speed reference | Automatic sizing, a palette, bars and donuts without path builders, and an accessibility layer, at a speed the budgets in section 5 keep honest |
docs/02-product-spec.md:29:### 1.2 Who it is for
docs/02-product-spec.md:31:A developer adding charts to a product or an internal dashboard: data arrives as rows from an API, the chart is one component among many on the page, and the person writing it is not a visualization specialist and will not test it with a screen reader. Coding agents writing that code are the same audience: they benefit from typed fields, one logical data model and diagnostics that say what to change.
docs/02-product-spec.md:35:### 1.3 Principles
docs/02-product-spec.md:40:| Say it, do not guess | Anything Axylo cannot draw faithfully becomes a diagnostic with a code, a location and a fix. If values were left out, the reader is told too. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:44:| The page is the theme | Font, text color and color scheme come from the page. |

## 6. Decisions and the findings behind them

### 1.5 Handle and commit contract

```ts
chart.update({ title: 'Sessions' });                 // options
chart.append([{ day: '2026-05-01', channel: 'Direct', sessions: 41210 }], { keep: 120 });   // rows
chart.zoom(['2026-03-01', '2026-03-31']);            // view
const off = chart.on('hover', point => { … });
chart.diagnostics;                                   // current, as soon as any call returns
chart.destroy();
```

Finding D3: the ten libraries have seven update idioms. Axylo has three methods, one per kind of change, with one contract.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Order | Calls are applied in the order made. `update({ data })` followed by `append` appends to the new data. |
| Two phases | Each call validates and normalizes synchronously: diagnostics are current when it returns, and a `strict` chart throws from that call. Drawing is deferred to the next animation frame, and calls made before that frame are drawn once. |
| Atomic switch | Marks, labels, hit testing and the accessibility layer move to a new data revision together. No frame mixes two revisions. |
| Patches | A key present in an `update` replaces the old value whole; a key set to `undefined` returns to its default; absent keys stay. No deep merging. |
| Rejected changes | A call that throws under `strict` leaves the chart on its last valid state. |
| Streaming | `keep` is the number of distinct x values retained. Rows before the last x are accepted through the slower full update and raise AX151. While zoomed to the latest edge the view follows new data; zoomed elsewhere, it stays put. Paused charts buffer (I6). Keyboard focus stays on its datum until that datum leaves the window (A7). |
| Teardown | `destroy()` cancels the pending frame, disconnects observers and listeners, and makes later calls no-ops. |

### 1.6 Diagnostics

The registry, with each code's level and outcome, is in the spec (section 3.5). Example for the Phase 1 combined dirty fixture (`[10, 20, null, NaN, '40', undefined, 70]`):

```
[axylo AX103] "Dirty input": y field "value" has 1 value that is not a finite number (NaN at row 3). Shown as a gap.
  Check the calculation that produced it, or send null for "no data".
[axylo AX106] "Dirty input": y field "value" mixes numbers with 1 string ("40" at row 4). The string is not plotted.
  Convert it to a number where the data is produced.
[axylo AX102] "Dirty input": y field "value" is absent in 1 row (row 5). Shown as a gap.
  Send null if the value is known to be missing.
```

The reader of that chart sees "Values not shown: 3. See table." (F12).

`validate(type, options)` runs the same normalization without a DOM and returns the diagnostics, so a server, a test or a coding agent can check a chart before rendering it.

Development and production flavours are selected through package `exports` conditions. The script-tag distribution ships `axylo.js` (development) and `axylo.min.js` (production). Errors and warnings print once per code per page in both; hints only in development.

### 1.7 React adapter (not in 1.0)

Removed from the first release by the owner on 2026-11-18: 1.0 is plain TypeScript, and adapters for React, Vue, Svelte and others follow later. The adapter described below was built, reviewed twice and fixed; its last state is `packages/react` at commit dac5664. The section is kept as the design to return to.

```tsx
import { Line } from '@axylo/react';

<Line data={rows} x="day" y="sessions" series="channel" title="Daily sessions by channel" />
```

| Behavior | Detail |
|---|---|
| Lifecycle | Create on mount, `destroy` on unmount; correct under StrictMode's setup, cleanup, setup. The file is marked `'use client'`. |
| Props to options | Field specs are compared structurally, so an inline `x={{ field: 'ts' }}` does not renormalize on every render. `data` is compared by identity; in development, the same content arriving three times with a new identity raises a hint to memoize it. |
| Removed props | A prop that disappears is sent as `undefined`, which restores the default. |
| Handlers | Replaced without recreating the chart. |
| Streaming | A ref exposes the handle, so `append`, `zoom` and `diagnostics` are reachable. When `data` is controlled, a new `data` prop replaces whatever was appended. |

The adapter is prototyped in M3, before the API freezes, because it is the cheapest way to find out whether the core contract survives a second consumer. It ships in 1.0 because finding 1.1 of the landscape shows where everyday charts are written; that is evidence of where charts are written, not of demand for Axylo.

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Pipeline

```
options ─► normalize ─► frame ──┬─► view model ─► layout ─► scene ─► mark renderer
            │ validate   (authoritative) │   scales, visible range         text renderer (DOM)
            ▼ diagnostics                ├─► lookup: exact values by x, by point, by ordinal
                                         ├─► summary and table
                                         └─► focus model
```

The **frame** is the normalized, lossless data: typed columns, a validity bitmap, dictionary-encoded categories, source-row indexes and a revision number. It is the only source for exact values. The table, the summary, keyboard navigation, tooltips and events read the frame. The **scene** is geometry for drawing and may be simplified (F5); nothing reads values back from it. The first draft derived accessibility from the scene, and two reviewers showed that a simplified drawing cannot return the samples it dropped.

| Stage | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| normalize | Frame, diagnostics | The only place raw input is read. Never coerces silently. |
| view model | Scales, visible index ranges, series visibility | Domain rules implement F1 and F7. |
| lookup | Nearest-x by binary search; nearest-point by a grid index (scatter) | Works on the frame within the visible range; cost bounded independently of the drawing. |
| layout | Plot rectangle, tick sets, label boxes, legend and control placement | Implements L1, L3, L8. Takes a text-measurement interface as input. |
| scene | Flat list of primitives (`path`, `rect`, `arc`, `rule`, `text`) | Plain data; testable in Node with injected text metrics. |
| renderers | Marks; DOM text; accessibility DOM | See 2.3. |

### 2.2 Invalidation

Stages are cached, and the cache keys are explicit. Caching on object identity alone, as the first draft said, would miss font loads, pixel-ratio changes and in-place mutation.

| Stage | Reruns when |
|---|---|
| normalize | Data revision or field encoding changes. `append` extends the frame without renormalizing earlier rows. |
| view model | Frame revision, zoom, series visibility, author domains. |
| layout | View model; container size; resolved font and text spacing; `document.fonts` finishing a load; locale; any label text. A data-only update reruns layout when the tick labels would change, and skips it otherwise. |
| scene | Layout or view model. |
| mark raster | Scene; device pixel ratio; resolved colors (L4's triggers). |

Text is measured with the page's computed font, letter spacing and word spacing applied to the measuring context, and layout reruns when fonts finish loading. The measurement interface is a parameter, so Node tests inject fixed metrics and browser tests use the real one.

### 2.3 Rendering

**Working assumption: Canvas 2D for marks, HTML for all text.** Text stays in the DOM so that it inherits the page font and color, honors user text spacing and zoom (A6), adapts in forced-colors mode, and can be selected and translated.

**This is reopened and decided in M1 by measurement.** The first draft justified canvas by Phase 1's slow SVG libraries, but those create a node per point; the one-path-per-series SVG chart in the harness was fast. With drawing simplified to a few vertices per pixel column (F5), an SVG path per series is small. SVG follows CSS variables and class-toggled themes with no repaint code, adapts to forced colors, prints sharply, needs no pixel-ratio handling and allocates no backing store (a 1,920×1,080 canvas at pixel ratio 2 is about 33 MB). Canvas is likely cheaper for per-frame redraw when streaming and hovering.

M1 builds both mark renderers behind the same scene and compares them on: P1, P2, P3, P5, bytes, memory, a runtime theme toggle, forced colors, print, and browser zoom. The scene is renderer-neutral either way, so the choice is contained.

**Simplified drawing.** Per device-pixel column and per contiguous run of valid samples, the stroke covers the run's minimum and maximum (F5). One rule for when it applies: more than four visible samples per device-pixel column on average. The pass over visible samples is O(visible) on typed columns and is measured separately from drawing; the vertex count is bounded by width times the number of runs, not by width alone.

**No animation system.** First render is not animated (I5). Updates cut, or tween for at most 200 ms where the cost is negligible, and not at all under reduced motion.

### 2.4 Document structure

```html
<figure class="axylo" id="ax7" role="group" aria-labelledby="ax7-t" aria-describedby="ax7-s">
  <figcaption>
    <h3 id="ax7-t">Daily sessions by channel</h3>        <!-- level from options; or omitted when labelledBy is used -->
    <p id="ax7-s" class="axylo-summary">Line chart, 3 series, …</p>
  </figcaption>
  <div class="axylo-plot" tabindex="0"> … marks … <div class="axylo-text" aria-hidden="true">tick labels</div></div>
  <div class="axylo-toolbar" role="toolbar" aria-label="Chart controls">   <!-- one tab stop, roving focus -->
    legend toggles · zoom in · zoom out · reset · pause · view as table
  </div>
  <p class="axylo-note" role="status">Values not shown: 2. See table.</p>
  <div class="axylo-live" aria-live="polite"></div>
  <div class="axylo-tooltip" hidden></div>
  <div class="axylo-table" hidden><!-- built when opened: caption, headers, pager --></div>
</figure>
```

Ids are generated per chart. The plot's role, and how a focused point is conveyed, are not fixed here: M1 runs a spike with three candidate patterns and M4 confirms the choice (section 4).

Default styles are applied without injecting a `<style>` element, and a standalone stylesheet ships for pages that prefer to load it themselves. Which mechanism passes a strict Content Security Policy is settled by the M7 test with real headers, not assumed.

## Historical M1 review and measurements

The table below is kept as measured. These statements made from it in the first version are withdrawn or narrowed:

- **Withdrawn: "nothing measured favours canvas except all-thread CPU during resize."** The recorded heap, DOM-node and layout counts also favour canvas.
- **Withdrawn: the resize CPU gap is raster work.** The number is CPU for the whole renderer process; no stage was traced.
- **Withdrawn: simplification bounds every chart by its width.** It was shown for line series only; point marks and many-series charts were not measured.
- **Withdrawn: an SVG theme change needs no run-time work.** Both renderers recorded six DOM mutations per toggle; "no canvas drawing call" is all that was observed.
- **Withdrawn: normalization and garbage collection explain the gap to uPlot.** About 71–73% of busy time in the production profiles is unmapped; the normalization share comes from development builds. It is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
- **Narrowed: "half the renderer memory."** The halving is of the increase above a data-only page at pixel ratio 2 (34.2 → 17.7 MiB). Absolute renderer memory was 74.7 → 56.2 MiB, and at pixel ratio 1 the increase was 23.1 → 18.4 MiB.
- **Narrowed: "no frame later than 25 ms."** True of the recorded animation-frame callbacks; the window can miss an interval that spans its boundary, and a callback is not a presented frame.
- **Void: every 24-chart page row** (page at pixel ratio 1 and 2, resize of the 24-chart page, and the memory row). The harness fix pass found that these runs drew no marks: at 230 × 115 px each tile is below the 120 × 80 px plot minimum of spec L8, so every chart showed its text fallback. The SVG records carry `svgPaths: 0`; the canvas runs held empty canvases. The numbers compare two empty charts and say nothing about the renderers. The harness now rejects a run whose chart drew no marks, and the page workload uses 340 × 200 px tiles.
- **Narrowed: verdicts.** 149 metric comparisons were judged without adjustment for choosing among them, on six pairs or fewer per workload, with noise bands from one session and two workload shapes. Two "SVG lower" rows allow a gain as small as 0.16 ms (10,000 points) and 6.3 ms (dashboard at pixel ratio 2).

Evidence: [bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md](../../bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md). One session of 39 runs, production build, headless Chrome 157, machine under load from other work, A-versus-A noise bands for two workloads only.

### What M1 measured

Canvas → SVG, medians of main-thread task time unless stated. "Lower" means the 95% interval cleared zero and the noise band where one existed.

| Workload | Canvas | SVG | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Streaming, per update | 2.26 ms | 1.45 ms | SVG lower |
| Theme change, per toggle | 2.68 ms and 27 drawing calls | 2.01 ms and no drawing call | SVG lower |
| Resize, one chart of 100,000 points | 915 ms | 472 ms | SVG lower on the main thread |
| Same, CPU across all threads | 1,035 ms | 1,770 ms | **SVG higher** |
| Resize, 24-chart page | 730 ms | 525 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
| First chart, 10,000 points | 34.0 ms | 28.4 ms | SVG lower |
| 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 199 ms | 158 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
| First chart, 3 × 120 | 23.6 ms | 19.8 ms | Inconclusive |
| First chart, 100,000 points | 81.8 ms | 83.5 ms | Inconclusive |
| First chart, 1,000,000 points | 622 ms | 652 ms | Inconclusive (4 blocks) |
| Memory, 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 34.2 MiB renderer, 11.5 MiB GPU, 7.7 MiB backing stores | 17.7 MiB, 2.2 MiB, none | Void: no marks were drawn |

No frame was later than 25 ms in any configuration, so frame pacing does not separate the two.

### Why SVG was the working default

1. On the line workloads measured, main-thread task time was lower with SVG or the two could not be told apart.
2. Line series are simplified to a few vertices per pixel column before either renderer sees them, so for line charts the path size follows the plot width, not the data.
3. SVG follows the page with less code: forced colors and print work through CSS, browser zoom stays sharp, and there is no backing store to size, cap or lose. This is a design argument, not a measurement.

### What M1 did not establish

- **GPU rasterization was not measured.** Headless Chrome here does not use a GPU. The resize, pixel-ratio-2 and process-memory results need a headed, GPU-backed rerun before they transfer.
- **Dense point marks were not measured.** A scatter chart with tens of thousands of markers is the case most likely to favour canvas.
- **One browser, one machine, one session.** Firefox and Safari may order the two differently.
- **Many series, pan and zoom, and the budget workloads P4, P7 and P8 were not measured**, and the million-point comparison has four pairs.
- Both renderers are far from uPlot in the configurations measured (about 80 ms against 12 ms at 100,000 points; uPlot draws no tooltip or accessibility layer). Where that time goes is not established.

A column made only of numeric strings yields AX104 and is drawn in full. `dirty-null` yields nothing.

The split between AX104 and AX106 answers a reviewer's objection that common back ends return counts as strings (Postgres `bigint` and `numeric`, BigQuery): a whole column of plain decimal strings is unambiguous and is parsed; a stray string among numbers is a bug and is not.

### 3.7 Compact variant

`compact: true` on line, area and bar draws the marks and nothing else: no axes, gridlines, legend, toolbar, table control, zoom or tooltip. It is for a small tile where the page already shows the number and the label.

| ID | Criterion | Verified by |
|---|---|---|

It has no tab stop and no pointer-only behavior, so nothing is available to a mouse that is not available to a keyboard. | Accessibility-tree snapshot; a page of 40 has zero added tab stops, WCAG 1.1.1 |

| C3 | It fills its container at any size from 24×16 CSS px up; with no definite height it is 32 px tall. | Size tests |
| C4 | With more than one series, lines differ by dash as well as color, and bars by fill pattern between neighbours (A5), since there is no legend; AX131 suggests one series per compact chart. | Two-series fixture, WCAG 1.4.1 |
| C5 | When values were left out (F12), the description says so and a small marker with a text equivalent appears in the corner. | `dirty` fixture in compact mode, WCAG 1.1.1 |

A compact chart does not give access to every value; the summary is its alternative. An author who needs every value reachable uses the full chart.

### 3.8 What the evidence will and will not show

Automated checks establish structure: names, roles, focus order, contrast, text. They do not establish that a screen-reader user finds a chart understandable. 1.0 has no evidence for that: no screen reader was run against it, not even by the developer (the owner's decision, 2026-11-18; the rehearsal on five reader and browser pairs that earlier drafts of this section planned was not done). Axylo is built by one person with no access to study participants, so no claim of usability testing with disabled users is made, and the conformance table says both things in those words. Reviewers proposed participant testing as a release gate; it is recorded here as a known limit instead.

These numbers are provisional. They are design targets taken from Phase 1's order-of-magnitude measurements, and they become release gates only after the benchmark harness built in M0 has measured a working Axylo slice in M1 and the limits have been recalibrated and frozen (plan, M1 and M6). 1. Budgets apply to default options. Finding D8 showed libraries that are fast only for authors who know which options to set.
2. Budgets are absolute, on named hardware profiles. Comparison libraries, uPlot above all, are measured in the same runs and published beside Axylo, but a ratio to another library is not a gate: it would reward leaving out work that library does not do.
3. The accessibility layer is on in every measured configuration.

## 6. Decisions and the findings behind them


| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Order | Calls are applied in the order made. `update({ data })` followed by `append` appends to the new data. |
| Two phases | Each call validates and normalizes synchronously: diagnostics are current when it returns, and a `strict` chart throws from that call. Drawing is deferred to the next animation frame, and calls made before that frame are drawn once. |
| Atomic switch | Marks, labels, hit testing and the accessibility layer move to a new data revision together. No frame mixes two revisions. |
| Patches | A key present in an `update` replaces the old value whole; a key set to `undefined` returns to its default; absent keys stay. No deep merging. |
| Rejected changes | A call that throws under `strict` leaves the chart on its last valid state. |
| Streaming | `keep` is the number of distinct x values retained. Rows before the last x are accepted through the slower full update and raise AX151. While zoomed to the latest edge the view follows new data; zoomed elsewhere, it stays put. Paused charts buffer (I6). Keyboard focus stays on its datum until that datum leaves the window (A7). |
| Teardown | `destroy()` cancels the pending frame, disconnects observers and listeners, and makes later calls no-ops. |

### 1.6 Diagnostics

The registry, with each code's level and outcome, is in the spec (section 3.5). Example for the Phase 1 combined dirty fixture (`[10, 20, null, NaN, '40', undefined, 70]`):

```
[axylo AX103] "Dirty input": y field "value" has 1 value that is not a finite number (NaN at row 3). Shown as a gap.
  Check the calculation that produced it, or send null for "no data".
[axylo AX106] "Dirty input": y field "value" mixes numbers with 1 string ("40" at row 4). The string is not plotted.
  Convert it to a number where the data is produced.
[axylo AX102] "Dirty input": y field "value" is absent in 1 row (row 5). Shown as a gap.
  Send null if the value is known to be missing.
```

The reader of that chart sees "Values not shown: 3. See table." (F12).

`validate(type, options)` runs the same normalization without a DOM and returns the diagnostics, so a server, a test or a coding agent can check a chart before rendering it.

### 2.2 Invalidation

Stages are cached, and the cache keys are explicit. Caching on object identity alone, as the first draft said, would miss font loads, pixel-ratio changes and in-place mutation.

| Stage | Reruns when |
|---|---|
| normalize | Data revision or field encoding changes. `append` extends the frame without renormalizing earlier rows. |
| view model | Frame revision, zoom, series visibility, author domains. |
| layout | View model; container size; resolved font and text spacing; `document.fonts` finishing a load; locale; any label text. A data-only update reruns layout when the tick labels would change, and skips it otherwise. |
| scene | Layout or view model. |
| mark raster | Scene; device pixel ratio; resolved colors (L4's triggers). |

Text is measured with the page's computed font, letter spacing and word spacing applied to the measuring context, and layout reruns when fonts finish loading. The measurement interface is a parameter, so Node tests inject fixed metrics and browser tests use the real one.

### 2.3 Rendering

**Working assumption: Canvas 2D for marks, HTML for all text.** Text stays in the DOM so that it inherits the page font and color, honors user text spacing and zoom (A6), adapts in forced-colors mode, and can be selected and translated.

**This is reopened and decided in M1 by measurement.** The first draft justified canvas by Phase 1's slow SVG libraries, but those create a node per point; the one-path-per-series SVG chart in the harness was fast. With drawing simplified to a few vertices per pixel column (F5), an SVG path per series is small. SVG follows CSS variables and class-toggled themes with no repaint code, adapts to forced colors, prints sharply, needs no pixel-ratio handling and allocates no backing store (a 1,920×1,080 canvas at pixel ratio 2 is about 33 MB). Canvas is likely cheaper for per-frame redraw when streaming and hovering.

M1 builds both mark renderers behind the same scene and compares them on: P1, P2, P3, P5, bytes, memory, a runtime theme toggle, forced colors, print, and browser zoom. The scene is renderer-neutral either way, so the choice is contained.

**Simplified drawing.** Per device-pixel column and per contiguous run of valid samples, the stroke covers the run's minimum and maximum (F5). One rule for when it applies: more than four visible samples per device-pixel column on average. The pass over visible samples is O(visible) on typed columns and is measured separately from drawing; the vertex count is bounded by width times the number of runs, not by width alone.

**No animation system.** First render is not animated (I5). Updates cut, or tween for at most 200 ms where the cost is negligible, and not at all under reduced motion.

### 2.4 Document structure

```html
<figure class="axylo" id="ax7" role="group" aria-labelledby="ax7-t" aria-describedby="ax7-s">
  <figcaption>
    <h3 id="ax7-t">Daily sessions by channel</h3>        <!-- level from options; or omitted when labelledBy is used -->
    <p id="ax7-s" class="axylo-summary">Line chart, 3 series, …</p>
  </figcaption>
  <div class="axylo-plot" tabindex="0"> … marks … <div class="axylo-text" aria-hidden="true">tick labels</div></div>
  <div class="axylo-toolbar" role="toolbar" aria-label="Chart controls">   <!-- one tab stop, roving focus -->
    legend toggles · zoom in · zoom out · reset · pause · view as table
  </div>
  <p class="axylo-note" role="status">Values not shown: 2. See table.</p>
  <div class="axylo-live" aria-live="polite"></div>
  <div class="axylo-tooltip" hidden></div>
  <div class="axylo-table" hidden><!-- built when opened: caption, headers, pager --></div>
</figure>
```

Ids are generated per chart. The plot's role, and how a focused point is conveyed, are not fixed here: M1 runs a spike with three candidate patterns and M4 confirms the choice (section 4).

Default styles are applied without injecting a `<style>` element, and a standalone stylesheet ships for pages that prefer to load it themselves. Which mechanism passes a strict Content Security Policy is settled by the M7 test with real headers, not assumed.

import type { BrowserContextOptions, Page } from 'playwright-core';
import { openEntry } from '../harness';
import { decodePng, type Image } from './png';
import { parseColor } from '../../../src/theme/color';
import { AXYLO_CSS as CURRENT } from '../../../src/theme/css';
import { AXYLO_CSS as PROPOSED } from './proposed-css';

const MARKER = '/* structure: added by the figure module';

/** The proposed token and mark part (proposed-css.ts) followed by the current structure part. */
export function proposedStylesheet(): string {
  return PROPOSED.slice(0, PROPOSED.indexOf(MARKER)) + CURRENT.slice(CURRENT.indexOf(MARKER));
}

export const ENTRY = 'packages/axylo/test/browser/render/entries/axylo-render.entry.ts';

/**
 * Opens the blank page with the render entry loaded. The page's two buttons are hidden so nothing sits
 * behind the marks.
 */
export async function open(options: BrowserContextOptions = {}): Promise<Page> {
  const page = await openEntry(ENTRY, options);
  await page.addStyleTag({ content: '#before, #after { display: none; }' });
  // AXYLO_PROPOSED_CSS=1 runs the suite against the proposed stylesheet, loaded as a standalone sheet.
  if (process.env.AXYLO_PROPOSED_CSS === '1') {
    await page.evaluate(css => { const s = document.createElement('style'); s.textContent = css; document.head.appendChild(s); }, proposedStylesheet());
  }
  return page;
}

export async function close(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const errors = (page as Page & { errors: string[] }).errors;
  await page.context().close();
  if (errors.length > 0) throw new Error(`page errors: ${errors.join('; ')}`);
}

/** Screenshot of a page region, decoded. At device scale factor k the image is k times the CSS size. */
export async function shot(page: Page, x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number): Promise<Image> {
  return decodePng(await page.screenshot({ clip: { x, y, width, height }, animations: 'disabled', caret: 'hide' }));
}

export type RGB = readonly [number, number, number];

export function at(img: Image, x: number, y: number): RGB {
  const o = (Math.floor(y) * img.width + Math.floor(x)) * 4;
  return [img.data[o]!, img.data[o + 1]!, img.data[o + 2]!];
}

export function rgb(color: string): RGB {
  const c = parseColor(color);
  if (c === null) throw new Error(`not a color: ${color}`);
  return [Math.round(c.r * 255), Math.round(c.g * 255), Math.round(c.b * 255)];
}

export const WHITE: RGB = [255, 255, 255];

/** Largest channel difference. */
export const diff = (a: RGB | readonly number[], b: RGB | readonly number[]): number =>
  Math.max(Math.abs(a[0]! - b[0]!), Math.abs(a[1]! - b[1]!), Math.abs(a[2]! - b[2]!));

/** `color` at `alpha` over `under`. */
export const blend = (color: RGB, alpha: number, under: RGB = WHITE): RGB =>
  [0, 1, 2].map(i => color[i]! * alpha + under[i]! * (1 - alpha)) as unknown as RGB;

export function ink(img: Image, x0: number, y0: number, x1: number, y1: number, background: RGB = WHITE, threshold = 40): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (let y = y0; y < y1; y++) for (let x = x0; x < x1; x++) if (diff(at(img, x, y), background) > threshold) n++;
  return n;
}

export const frames = (page: Page, n = 2): Promise<void> => page.evaluate(k => window.axr.frames(k), n);
describe('RectMark.pattern (spec F9 second cue)', () => {
  it('a patterned bar differs from a plain bar of the same color in SVG', async () => {
    const page = await open();
    await page.evaluate(() => { window.axr.mount(460, 60, { scene: 'pattern' }); });
    const img = await shot(page, 460, 60, 400, 300);
    // Pixels of a bar's interior (2 px in from each edge) that differ from the plain bar's colour by more than a
    // quarter of the range (64/255): what F9 needs is a pattern that stands clear of the bar's own colour. Not
    // "close to the background": how far a 1 px line or a radius-1 dot gets towards it is the engine's
    // anti-aliasing (a dot's pixels reach 52/255 from white in Chrome, 106/255 in WebKit).
    const plainColor = (img: Image): RGB => at(img, 90, 150);
    const marked = (img: Image, x0: number): number => {
      const plain = plainColor(img);
      let n = 0;
      for (let y = 62; y < 238; y++) for (let x = x0 + 2; x < x0 + 58; x++) if (diff(at(img, x, y), plain) > 64) n++;
      return n;
    };
    expect(diff(plainColor(img), WHITE), 'the plain bar is painted').toBeGreaterThan(64);
    expect(marked(img, 60)).toBe(0);
    const diagonal = marked(img, 140), cross = marked(img, 220), dots = marked(img, 300);
    // About 1 px lines every 5.7 px: roughly a sixth of the area, twice that for the cross hatch.
    expect(diagonal).toBeGreaterThan(800);
    expect(cross).toBeGreaterThan(diagonal * 1.4);
    expect(dots).toBeGreaterThan(150);
    // Patterns stay inside their bars.
    expect(ink(img, 122, 60, 138, 240)).toBe(0);
    await close(page);
  });
});

describe('RectMark.pattern on SVG: the element that carries the series colour carries the pattern (spec C4, F9)', () => {
  it('each patterned bar has an element painted with its series colour whose fill is the pattern', async () => {
    const page = await open();
    await page.evaluate(() => { window.axr.mount(20, 60, { scene: 'pattern' }); });
    const cues = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const out: string[] = [];
      for (const el of document.querySelectorAll<SVGElement>('svg *')) {
        if (!el.style.getPropertyValue('color')) continue;
        const fill = getComputedStyle(el).fill;
        if (fill.startsWith('url')) out.push(el.tagName);
      }
      return out;
    });
    // Three patterned bars (diagonal, cross, dots), each repeated once as its pattern overlay.
    expect(cues.length).toBe(3);
    expect(cues.every(tag => tag === 'rect')).toBe(true);
    await close(page);
  });
});
